children: Traders see the odds of the Fed hiking rates this month as more or less a coin toss.
They are pricing a roughly 50% chance of a quarter-point increase, according to CME data. Only yesterday, investors were pricing a 70% likelihood of a hike.

That's after prominent Fed board members spoke out to dispel the notion that a rate rise was a foregone conclusion: Christopher Waller just now said he would support holding rates steady if August data shows inflation continues to make progress, a day after John Williams said the case for a hike wasn't firm.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
